note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in AL.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Alabama's Coastal Connection
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (listed by the program as a national byway)
byways.where: Mobile and Baldwin counties: Bayou La Batre, Dauphin Island, Mobile Bay Ferry to Fort Morgan, Gulf Shores, Orange Beach, Foley

facts.fact: The national byway is 130 miles long.
Forts Gaines and Morgan, National Historic Landmarks, stand on either side of the mouth of Mobile Bay.

The Mobile Bay Ferry is an auto ferry between Fort Gaines and Fort Morgan; the byway passes through Bayou La Batre, where the Blessing of the Fleet is held on the first Sunday in May; Bon Secour National Wildlife Refuge has about 7,000 acres of habitat.

byways.name: The Appalachian Highlands Scenic Byway
byways.where: AL 9 from I-20 near Heflin via Piedmont and Centre, US 411 to Leesburg, AL 273 to Blanche, AL 35 over Lookout Mountain to Fort Payne and I-59; Cleburne, Calhoun, Cherokee and DeKalb counties

facts.fact: About 80 miles long, connecting I-20 near Heflin with I-59 at Fort Payne through Cleburne, Calhoun, Cherokee and DeKalb counties.
Follows AL 9 through the Talladega National Forest, White Plains, Piedmont, Ellisville and Centre, past cotton fields, then US 411, AL 273 and AL 35.
AL 35 climbs Lookout Mountain and passes through Little River Canyon National Preserve before descending to Fort Payne.

byways.name: Barbour County Governors' Trail
byways.where: AL 51 / SR 10 junction at Clio, northeast via Louisville to Clayton, AL 30 to Eufaula, US 431 north to the Shorter Mansion; Barbour County

facts.fact: Designated by legislative act in 2000 to honor Barbour County's governors: John Gill Shorter, William Dorsey Jelks, Braxton Bragg Comer, Chauncey Sparks, George C. Wallace and Lurleen B. Wallace.
Begins in Clio at SR 10 and SR 51, runs through Louisville to Clayton, follows SR 30 to Eufaula and ends at the Shorter Mansion on US 431; about 36 miles.
Nearby are Blue Springs State Park with its spring-fed pool and Lake Eufaula.

byways.name: The Black Belt Nature and Heritage Trail
byways.where: Network of loops across 13 west-central Alabama counties (Livingston-Aliceville, Demopolis-Marion, Selma-Camden and Tuskegee-Union Springs loops)

facts.fact: The Black Belt is named for the rich black soil that grew cotton in the 19th century; the trail's tours cover more than 50 sites in 13 counties.
Ezell's Fish Camp, known for fried catfish, is on the Livingston-Aliceville Loop; Moundville is on the Demopolis-Marion Loop.
Gaineswood in Demopolis was built by owner-architect Nathan Bryan Whitfield over eighteen years, 1843 to 1861.

byways.review: A trail of several loops rather than one road; the catalog line (217 mi) should be checked against the loops.

byways.name: Black Warrior River Scenic Byway
byways.where: About 12 miles of city streets along both banks of the Black Warrior River in Tuscaloosa and Northport, Tuscaloosa County

facts.fact: An urban route of about 12 miles along the Black Warrior River with three river bridges.
The route passes the site of the Alabama State Capitol from 1826 to 1847 and borders the Tuscaloosa and Northport riverwalks.
The restored Queen City Pool and Bathhouse on the route houses the Mildred Westervelt Warner Transportation Museum.

byways.review: Not in the catalog and no agency GIS line; exact streets are not listed on the program page (gateways are I-59/20 exits 71 and 73, US 82, US 43 and US 69).

byways.name: Leeds Stagecoach Route
byways.where: Old Ashville-to-Montevallo stagecoach road through Leeds, from the Shelby County side near Lake Purdy north toward Moody; Jefferson, Shelby and St. Clair counties

facts.fact: The route began as an Indian trail, was widened by Andrew Jackson's scouts in 1812-13, and became a stagecoach route after settlers arrived in Leeds in 1820.
Local tradition and John Garst's studies place John Henry's contest with the steam drill at the C&W Railroad's Oak Tunnel in Leeds in the 1880s.
The byway runs about eighteen miles through a valley of horse farms and historic homes; Leeds parks sit on the Little Cahaba River.

byways.review: The program page gives about 18 miles; the catalog line maps only 7 miles.

byways.name: Lookout Mountain Parkway
byways.where: Lookout Mountain from Gadsden north via Fort Payne and Mentone toward the Georgia line (the parkway continues to Chattanooga); Etowah, Cherokee and DeKalb counties

facts.fact: The parkway spans three states across Lookout Mountain from Gadsden, Alabama to Chattanooga, Tennessee, about 93 miles.
Each August the World's Longest Yard Sale lines the parkway with vendors.
Little River Canyon National Preserve, DeSoto State Park and Cloudmont ski area at Mentone are along or near the Alabama route.

byways.review: The association gives 93 miles for all three states, but the catalog maps 104 miles in Alabama alone; check the catalog line.

byways.name: The Natchez Trace Parkway
byways.designation: All-American Road; first designated in Alabama through the Legislature and Governor
byways.where: Mileposts about 309 to 341, Colbert and Lauderdale counties, crossing the Tennessee River

facts.fact: The parkway runs 444 miles through three states, roughly following the Old Natchez Trace.
The parkway has 33 miles in Alabama; Freedom Hills Overlook at milepost 317 is the parkway's highest point in Alabama.
At Colbert Ferry, milepost 327.3, the Chickasaw George Colbert ran a ferry on the Tennessee River from 1800 to 1819 and kept an inn nearby.

byways.name: Selma to Montgomery Historic Trail
byways.designation: All-American Road (Selma to Montgomery March Byway); first designated through the Legislature and Governor
byways.where: US 80 from the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma through Lowndes County to the State Capitol in Montgomery; Dallas, Lowndes and Montgomery counties

facts.fact: The national historic trail is 54 miles long, with visitor centers in Selma, Lowndes County and Montgomery.
The first march on March 7, 1965 was stopped at the Edmund Pettus Bridge; the final march left Selma on March 21 and ended at the Capitol in Montgomery.
The byway follows the 1965 Selma to Montgomery March route and passes through the countryside where marchers camped overnight.

byways.review: The program lists it as 'Selma to Montgomery Historic Trail'; FHWA names it the Selma to Montgomery March Byway.

byways.name: Talladega Scenic Drive
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway; first designated through the Legislature and Governor
byways.where: AL 281 from US 78 west of Heflin through Cheaha State Park to Adams Gap and FSR 600; Cleburne and Clay counties, Talladega National Forest

facts.fact: The drive starts at US 78 and SR 281 west of Heflin, follows SR 281 through the Talladega National Forest and Cheaha Wilderness, and ends where the pavement ends at Adams Gap and Forest Service Road 600.
The road climbs to 2,407 feet at Alabama's highest point.
SR 281 runs the crest of the Talladega Mountains and was originally an unpaved forest route called the Skyway Motorway.

byways.review: Length given as 26.4 miles by FHWA and 29 miles by the Forest Service.

byways.name: Tensaw Parkway
byways.designation: Alabama Scenic Byway (listed by the program; its own page still calls it 'proposed')
byways.where: AL 225 and AL 59 along the eastern edge of the Mobile-Tensaw Delta, Spanish Fort north via Stockton toward Tensaw; Baldwin County

facts.fact: The parkway follows the State Highway 225/59 corridor along the eastern edge of the Mobile-Tensaw River Delta in north Baldwin County.
Fourteen boat landings are reached from just off the corridor; Historic Blakeley State Park and Fort Mims State Memorial Park lie along it.
SR 225 runs 24 miles from US 31 at Spanish Fort to SR 59 at Stockton.

byways.review: Not in the catalog and no agency GIS line. Endpoints on SR 59 are not stated by the program.

issues: The program site (alabamabyways.com) was last edited around 2014-2018 and its byway pages are 2012-2013 posts; no newer list was found, so designations after 2014 (if any) would be missed. Web search budget was exhausted, so no independent current list was checked.
Tensaw Parkway is filed under State Byways and counted among the 7 state byways on the home page, but its own page calls it the 'proposed Tensaw Parkway'; confirm it was actually designated.

Black Warrior River Scenic Byway and Tensaw Parkway are not in the catalog and have no GIS line; they cannot be drawn without hand digitizing (Tensaw roughly AL 225 Spanish Fort to Stockton plus AL 59; Black Warrior a ~12-mile riverside loop in Tuscaloosa/Northport).
Leeds Stagecoach Route: program says about 18 miles, catalog maps 7.
Lookout Mountain Parkway: the association says 93 miles across three states, yet the catalog maps 104 miles in Alabama; the catalog line may include extra roads.

Natchez Trace and Selma to Montgomery: the program site files them under National Byways; the history page says they (with Talladega) were designated as state byways via the Legislature and Governor before the 2000 act. Coastal Connection is also listed as a national byway; its state designation date is not stated.
Talladega Scenic Drive length differs: FHWA 26.4 mi, USFS 29 mi, catalog 26 mi.
